newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end low, turnover led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end low, turnover led by blue chips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks continued a correction with local investors booking profit and turnover supported by foreign buying of blue chips, brokers said.

The all share index closed 2.67 points down at 626.62. Despite significant gains by two highly-capitalised blue chips, 37 price declines outweighed 12 gains. Blue chips John Keells Holdings rose four rupees to 175, National Development Bank two to 195. Bairaha Farms fell 1.25 to 13.
"We had to pay up to source the quantities of blue chips foreigners wanted, even though it was against the market trend of falling prices," said a broker who asked not to be named.
Turnover was 45.5 million rupees on 801,161 shares. The main trades were foreign buying of 17,400 Development Finance, 19,200 John Keells Holdings and 102,600 National Development Bank.

"Though there will be some selective buying, overall buying will return only after investors have clearly seen where prices will settle after the profit-taking," said Dimantha Kohombanwickremage, a trader at NDBS Stock Brokers.
Trading in Pure Beverages, which was suspended following an unusual 24 percent price gain on Tuesday, will recommence on Friday, the stock exchange said.
